chunks: Al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿĀmir al-Qaṣabānī narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And the mothers shall suckle their children for two full years."

He عليه السلام said: "So long as the child is in suckling, it is shared equally between the two parents. Then when it is weaned, the father has more right to it than the mother. Then if the father dies, the mother has more right to it than the agnatic relatives. And if the father finds someone to suckle him for four dirhams, and the mother says, 'I will not suckle him except for five dirhams,' then he has the right to remove him from her, except that it is better for him and gentler for the child that he leave him with his mother."

key_terms.الرَّضَاعِ: the period of suckling or breastfeeding
key_terms.الْوَالِدَاتُ: the mothers, specifically in the context of breastfeeding and maternal care
key_terms.حَوْلَيْنِ كَامِلَيْنِ: two complete years, indicating the full nursing period
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: dirhams, used here as payment for nursing

ai.seo_question: Who has more right to custody of a child during nursing and after weaning in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal implications of the verse on suckling by outlining custodial priority during nursing and after weaning. It states that both parents share equal right while the child is nursing, then the father has greater right after weaning, and if the father dies, the mother takes precedence over paternal relatives. It also addresses payment for nursing and affirms that remaining with the mother may be better and gentler for the child.
